skill.name: ai-image-generation
skill.description: Generate hosted images through the Luxin CLI and API without configuring a provider account. The workflow supports guided setup, spending limits, recoverable jobs, hosted media, and cost receipts.
skill.summary: Create hosted AI images through Luxin with guided setup, cost controls, and recoverable jobs.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed six external command findings, two external API findings, and three hidden configuration path findings. Thirteen Markdown and documentation matches were false positives. Semantic review found remote-generated command execution, mutable hosted contracts, global self-installation, and external data disclosure risks.

remediation.issue: The examples execute unpinned npm packages with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every npm package to a reviewed version and publish integrity information. Remove automatic confirmation from installation examples.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to execute data.next_command returned by a hosted service.
remediation.suggestion: Return structured actions from an allowlist. Require explicit human approval before converting any hosted response into a shell command.

remediation.issue: The skill delegates behavior to mutable remote skill, LLM, and CLI contracts.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed contract or pin remote content by immutable version and hash. Reaudit every contract update.

remediation.issue: Installation examples write to global or hidden agent configuration with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Use workspace-local installation by default. Explain every modified path and require confirmation before changing agent configuration.

remediation.issue: Hosted media and feedback can disclose prompts, commands, or task details.
remediation.suggestion: Document retention and deletion behavior. Redact credentials and sensitive prompt content before uploads or feedback submission.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses Markdown backticks around the Luxin name. It contains no Ruby backtick operator or shell execution.
The detected backticks format response field names in prose. The separate instruction to run a returned command is covered as a semantic finding.
The fenced block executes luxin-cli through npx with automatic confirmation and the mutable latest version. This grants newly downloaded package code the user's permissions.
This range contains a Markdown fence terminator, headings, and another fence marker. Those delimiters do not execute a command.
The block runs an unpinned luxin-cli package through npx with automatic confirmation. A compromised current release could execute arbitrary code.
This range contains Markdown fence markers and installation prose but no command body. The following executable block has its own finding.
The block invokes npx to install a community skill at full depth, globally, and without confirmation. It can modify agent configuration and introduce unreviewed content.
This range contains a closing Markdown fence and explanatory text. It does not contain Ruby or shell backtick execution.
The fenced command invokes npx to perform a global, full-depth skill installation with automatic confirmation. That is a real external command with persistent configuration effects.
The detected text is a Markdown fence followed by prose about installation paths. No shell substitution or command execution occurs in this range.
Backticks only format HOME and CODEX_HOME path names. The line does not use the shell backtick execution operator.
This shell block changes HOME and CODEX_HOME, creates directories, and runs an automatic global skill installation. These commands alter agent state and execute downloaded tooling.
The range ends with an instruction to run the Luxin feedback command. It is a real external command that transmits task details to a hosted service.
This HTTPS URL is homepage metadata. It does not itself initiate a request or expose data.
This is an HTTPS documentation reference in metadata, not an outbound request. Risks from relying on mutable remote contracts are covered separately.
The URL is declared as metadata and does not perform network access by itself. The mutable remote contract risk is covered as a semantic finding.
The declared hosted API is the service endpoint used for image generation. Using this skill creates an external network trust boundary for prompts and generated media.
This HTTPS link is a documentation reference and does not itself send data. Delegation to mutable remote instructions is addressed separately.
This is a link to an LLM contract, not executable network code. The security impact of remotely mutable instructions is captured as a semantic finding.
This is a documented HTTPS CLI contract URL. A literal documentation URL alone is not a network vulnerability.
This is the hosted API endpoint that receives image generation requests. It represents real third-party network access and data disclosure.
The prose explicitly states that the installer writes agent state under $HOME/.agents. Modifying hidden agent configuration can persist changes across tasks.
The shell command redirects HOME to a hidden workspace directory before installation. Downstream tools can then write configuration and state there.
The command directs Codex profile state to a hidden .codex directory that is created on the next line. This is intentional hidden configuration access.

content.user_title: Generate Hosted AI Images with Luxin
content.value_statement: Image generation often requires provider accounts, credentials, and separate billing. This skill uses Luxin commands to create hosted images with job recovery and cost controls.
actual_capabilities: Starts with a no-spend guide before image creation.
Creates images through the hosted Luxin runtime using a selected model and prompt.
Applies an estimated spending limit to each image request.
Produces durable hosted media with recoverable job information.
Provides cost receipts, model parameters, stable responses, and hosted feedback.
limitations: The workflow depends on Luxin, npm availability, and network access.
Prompts and generated media leave the local environment and use hosted storage.
Image creation can consume credits or trigger payment after user approval.
The contract is marked as preview, so models and payment options may change.

use_cases.title: Create Design Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate hosted concept images from a written brief while applying a clear spending limit.

use_cases.title: Add Images to Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Create recoverable image jobs that another agent can locate and cite later.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Visuals
use_cases.description: Explore product image directions without configuring separate provider credentials or local model infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image of [subject] in [style]. Use the no-spend guide first and ask before any paid generation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one image with a clear approval boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Sized Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [dimensions] image for [channel]. Show [subject], use [palette], and keep the estimated cost below [amount].
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs an image for a specific publishing format.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [count] distinct concepts for [product]. Vary composition and lighting while preserving [brand requirements], then summarize each hosted result.
prompt_templates.scenario: A design team wants controlled concept exploration.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Recoverable Production Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate production images from [brief] using [model]. Preserve job details, model parameters, cost receipts, and hosted references for later agents.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced workflow needs traceable outputs and recovery information.

output_examples.input: Create a square editorial image of a compact field camera on a stainless workbench.
output_examples.output: A hosted square image showing the camera, plus a concise summary of the model, job status, estimated cost, and recovery reference.

output_examples.input: Develop three product image concepts with soft studio lighting and a maximum cost of seven cents each.
output: Concept one uses a centered product view with a neutral background.
Concept two uses an angled close view with visible material detail.
Concept three uses a wider contextual composition with restrained props.

best_practices: Run the no-spend guide and review missing inputs before creating media.
Set a per-image spending limit and require approval before paid generation.
Remove sensitive details from prompts and feedback sent to the hosted service.
anti_patterns: Do not execute a hosted next command without inspecting and approving its exact action.
Do not use mutable package versions in unattended or privileged environments.
Do not place credentials, private source material, or personal data in prompts or feedback.

faq.question: Does this skill require a provider API key?
faq.answer: No provider key is required. The workflow uses the hosted Luxin runtime and may use an optional restricted Luxin token.

faq.question: Can I check readiness without spending credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with the guide and use its recommended no-spend action until creation is ready and approved.

faq.question: Can image generation cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. Creation can consume Luxin credits or use a payment flow. Set a spending limit and approve paid work explicitly.

faq.question: Where are generated images stored?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable hosted media stored with Luxin. Review Luxin retention and deletion terms before submitting sensitive material.

faq.question: Can another agent recover a previous job?
faq.answer: The documented workflow provides recoverable jobs and hosted references. Preserve the returned job information for later use.

faq.question: What happens when Luxin lacks a required capability?
faq.answer: Use a fallback only for the missing capability. Remove sensitive details before sending attempted commands or behavior through hosted feedback.
